comment: Which of vercel/next.js's own e2e tests the compatibility harness runs against cdk-nextjs.
Passed to the harness as NEXT_EXTERNAL_TESTS_FILTERS (see .github/workflows/e2e-harness.yml) and
read by next.js's test/get-test-filter.js: `rules.include`/`rules.exclude` are minimatch globs over
test file paths, and `suites[file].failed` lists individual test-case names to skip within a file
that is otherwise run.
`rules.include` is deliberately an explicit list rather than next.js's own
`test/e2e/**/*.test.{t,j}s{,x}`: every file still costs a `next build` of its fixture plus a deploy.
Those deploys are cheap but not free - all files share one stack (`hrns-shared`), created once by
scripts/e2e-warm.sh and then updated per file with `cdk deploy --hotswap-fallback`, which is ~1-2
minutes rather than the ~4 a fresh CloudFront distribution takes. Files run serialized (`-c 1`) for
that reason. The full tree would still be a thousand-plus builds, so widen this list as the adapter
earns it; see scripts/e2e-harness/README.md.
Every file listed here has been run against a real deployment and observed to pass. Add nothing on
the assumption that it will - the first version of this list was three files, all of which turned
out to be unbuildable by cdk-nextjs (see `excluded-notes`). Any case cdk-nextjs fails for its own
reasons is a bug to fix, not a `failed` entry. Once it has a verdict in docs/harness-coverage.md
saying the failure is acceptable, put the file in `suites` with those case names in `failed` and a
`comment` saying which verdict - that runs the rest of the file, which is the point. Whole files
left out entirely get their reason in `excluded-notes` instead.
docs/harness-coverage.md is the human-readable companion to this file: every screened file, its
outcome, and for each failure an explanation plus a verdict on whether it is a bug or acceptable.
6 of 8 cases. A file in `suites` is included with its named cases skipped,
which is next.js's own mechanism for a partially passing file - see
test/get-test-filter.js. The two skipped cases refresh the browser within
`retry`'s 3s default window after a `revalidatePath`, which is shorter than a
CloudFront invalidation takes; see docs/harness-coverage.md.
failed: app-dir trailingSlash handling should revalidate a page with generated static params (withSlash=true)
app-dir trailingSlash handling should revalidate a page with generated static params (withSlash=false)

comment: 3 of 5 cases. The two skipped ones assert that the first dynamic RSC request
after a tag revalidation still returns *stale* data. Next.js tracks tag
staleness in an in-process Map (tags-manifest.external.ts), so a distributed
cache handler has no way to say "stale, serve it anyway" - ours is
immediately fresh instead. Unreachable rather than broken; see
docs/harness-coverage.md.
failed: resume-data-cache should have consistent data between static and dynamic renders with use cache
resume-data-cache should have consistent data between static and dynamic renders with fetch cache

comment: 3 of 7 cases. The four skipped ones request a path with *unencoded* square
brackets (`/blog/[slug]`), which CloudFront rejects itself:
`400`, `content-length: 0`, `x-cache: Error from cloudfront` - the Lambda
never sees the request. Percent-encoded, the same route is correct
(`/blog/%5Bslug%5D` renders `[slug]`), so nothing on the cdk-nextjs side is
wrong. See docs/harness-coverage.md.

edge runtime, generally: cdk-nextjs refuses at build time to deploy any output whose runtime is not `nodejs`
(`assertNodeRuntimes` in src/adapter/build-outputs.ts). That is a deliberate product limitation -
the edge runtime is deprecated in Next.js, and cdk-nextjs supports Next.js 16's Node-runtime
The check throws during `next build`, so a fixture containing *any* edge route or legacy
middleware fails wholesale and per-case `failed` entries cannot rescue it. Such files have to be
left out of `rules.include` entirely. 931 of next.js's 1134 e2e files are edge-free (see the
`screening` block), so this is not much of a constraint on widening the list.
test/e2e/app-dir/app-static/app-static.t: Excluded: ~10 `*-edge` routes declare `export const runtime = 'edge'`. See the note above.
Worth revisiting as a source of individual cases to port, since it is the densest coverage of the
ISR/caching behavior cdk-nextjs's cache handler implements.
test/e2e/app-dir/actions/app-action.test: Excluded: the fixture ships a legacy edge `middleware.js`. See the note above.
Excluded: the fixture ships a legacy edge `middleware.js`. See the note above.
revalidation behind the CDN, two files: Excluded as timing-inherent, not as a cdk-nextjs defect:
The two skipped `trailingslash` cases in `suites` are the same problem.
Each loads a prerendered page, calls a route handler that runs `revalidatePath`/`revalidateTag`,
asserts the handler returned `revalidated: true` (it does), refreshes and expects new content.
The refresh is served from the CloudFront edge: a prerendered app-router page comes back
with `cache-control: s-maxage=31536000` and the second request to it reports `x-cache: Hit from
cloudfront` (verified by hand against a harness deployment).
cdk-nextjs does invalidate the edge on explicit revalidation (`invalidateCloudFrontPaths` in
src/adapter/s3-cache-handler.ts, and see docs/caching-guide.md) - including for a build-time
prerender, as of the `_N_T_` implicit-tag fix - but fire-and-forget: `CreateInvalidation` has no
bounded completion SLA. What decides whether a case survives that is how long it waits, and
`retry()` in next.js's test/lib/next-test-utils.ts defaults to 3000ms. segment-cache/
prefetch-inlining passes 15000 and is in `rules.include`; these take the default, or re-request
immediately. Vercel purges its own CDN synchronously as part of the revalidate, which is why the
tests are not gated out of deploy mode upstream.
test/e2e/app-dir/prerender-encoding/prer: Excluded as unsupported, and NOT an encoding bug - encoding is handled correctly. The fixture sets
`export const dynamicParams = false`, which cdk-nextjs does not support; see
With that flag Next.js gates the route's `routing.dynamicRoutes` entries behind preview cookies
expected to serve the concrete prerendered paths off the CDN itself and 404 everything else.
cdk-nextjs registers only dynamic *templates* in `manifest.pathnames` (`addPrerenderTemplates` in
src/adapter/build-outputs.ts), so with the gate in place nothing matches and every param 404s -
`/plain` as much as `/sticks%20%26%20stones`. Remove the flag from the fixture and both resolve.
Supporting it means routing concrete prerendered paths to the owning entrypoint while still
supplying the template's `nxtP*` params, which `addPrerenderTemplates` documents as the reason it
test/e2e/app-dir/asset-prefix/asset-pref: Excluded as an OPEN BUG, not as acceptable: 2 of 7 cases fail reproducibly because cdk-nextjs does
not serve `${assetPrefix}/_next/static/…`. Routing is fine - the failing assertions live in an
un-awaited `bundles.forEach(async …)`, which is why jest reports them against the rewrite cases.
With `assetPrefix: '/custom-asset-prefix'` Next.js emits script srcs under that prefix, while the
build's `staticFiles` keys stay unprefixed and the Lambda package has no `.next/static` at all (the
assets live in S3 behind CloudFront's `_next/static*` behavior). The prefixed URL misses that
behavior, falls through to the compute's default behavior, is rewritten to `/_next/static/…` and
404s. See docs/harness-coverage.md for the measurement and the two candidate fixes.
test/e2e/app-dir/segment-cache/refresh/s: Not excluded by us, and there is nothing to run: the file is `describe.skip` upstream, commented
`Disabled because too flaky`. Recorded so it is not re-screened - it reports "passing" in about 5
test/e2e/app-dir/segment-cache/cdn-cache: Not excluded by us: next.js itself skips this file under `isNextDeploy`. Listed only as a worked
example of the README's claim that deploy mode gates out what cannot work behind a CDN.
skipDeployment, 236 files: `nextTestSetup({ skipDeployment: true })` makes next.js replace the entire file with
`it.only('should skip next deploy')` and set `skipped`, so the file early-returns. jest then
reports it as passing in about 4 seconds having deployed nothing - the same false-coverage trap as
`describe.skip`, which is why screen.mjs now disqualifies it. 236 of what were previously counted
as candidates are in this class, and two files (app-dir/not-found-default,
app-dir/use-cache-search-params) had been added to `rules.include` on the strength of such a pass;
both have been removed. Eleven more were tried in one batch before the screen existed:
A file that 'finishes' in under ~10s deployed nothing. Read the duration, not the exit code.

comment: Regenerate with `node scripts/e2e-harness/screen.mjs --next ../next.js --write`,
and `--check` to verify these numbers still hold. Not read by next.js's
test/get-test-filter.js, which only looks at `version`, `suites` and `rules`.
`candidates` is what is left after the screens below, all of which are
explained in scripts/e2e-harness/README.md. A candidate is a file worth
spending a deploy on - not a file expected to pass. Nothing enters
`rules.include` until it has been watched to pass against a real deployment,
and anything that fails gets a verdict in docs/harness-coverage.md.
`included-in-part` counts files in `suites`: run, minus the cases named in
their `failed` arrays. They are excluded from `candidates` too.
`disqualified-by` counts overlap - a fixture can ship edge middleware *and*
be skipped upstream - so the values sum to more than `e2e-files` minus
`candidates` minus `included`.
